official.deadline_note: Stage 1 concept notes must be submitted by Friday, October 30, 2026, 23:59 GMT, by email to clp.applications@birdlife.org. Late, incomplete or ineligible submissions will not be considered. Stage 2 has no published date - only shortlisted (highest-scoring) concept note applicants are notified and invited to submit a full application through the online portal.
official.status_note: The award page states: 'The call for applications to the CLP Future Conservationist Awards 2027 is open.'
benefits: A project grant of up to US$15,000 for the proposed conservation project
Ongoing support through CLP's global Alumni Network, including funding, training and mentorship
eligibility: All team members must be early in their careers, i.e. have no more than five years of professional conservation experience
Project teams must include at least three people and explain how each team member will develop their capacity through the project
All team members must be nationals of the country in which the project will take place, although one team member can be a non-national if this is clearly justified
Projects must take place in an eligible country (see guidelines) and project duration must be between six and 12 months
Proposed projects must go beyond academic research, demonstrated through both ecological research and conservation action on globally important, at-risk habitats and species
The total funding request from CLP must not exceed US$15,000 and CLP funding must cover at least 50% of the project budget

official.application_route: Email a completed concept note on the official template to clp.applications@birdlife.org by the Stage 1 deadline; shortlisted teams then submit a full application via the CLP online portal.
official.citizenship_residency: All team members must be nationals of the country in which the project will take place; one team member may be a non-national if this is clearly justified.
official.international_eligibility: Open to teams worldwide provided the project takes place in an eligible country listed in the guidelines.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Projects must deliver effective conservation interventions for globally important, at-risk habitats and species through both ecological research and conservation action within one of eight themes: a) climate impact and adaptation, b) biodiversity conservation, c) habitat restoration and/or management, d) social development and wellbeing, e) Indigenous community participation and/or community-led conservation, f) environmental policy, g) human-wildlife conflict, or h) environmental education and citizen science. 'At-risk' means IUCN Red List globally threatened (Critically Endangered, Endangered, Vulnerable) or Data Deficient, or where information indicates the need for urgent local conservation action.
official.research_requirement: Proposed projects must go beyond academic research and this must be demonstrated in the application.
official.duration: Project duration must be between six and 12 months.
official.description: Annual CLP Future Conservationist Awards offer early-career conservationists a project grant of up to $15,000 as well as ongoing support through CLP's global Alumni Network, including funding, training and mentorship. For 2027 the process runs in two stages: a concept note first, then a full application from shortlisted concepts only.

verification.notes: Read the Conservation Leadership Programme's own award page in full on 2026-10-10; the open 2027 call, the up-to-$15,000 grant, the 50% minimum CLP budget share, the eligibility criteria, the eight themes and the 30 October 2026 (23:59 GMT) Stage 1 deadline are all confirmed as published.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a team project grant rather than a study scholarship: you need at least two collaborators, every member early in their career (five years or less of professional conservation experience) and a national of the country where the work happens, with only one justified exception allowed. Stage 1 is only a concept note on the official template sent by email, and only the highest-scoring concepts see Stage 2, so the template and the eight themes do the real filtering. Because CLP must cover at least 50% of the budget, a credible co-funding plan is a precondition, not an afterthought.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Early-career national conservationists in an eligible country who already have a small team and an applied, measurable project on threatened species or habitats that is too small for larger funders.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm the project country appears on the eligible-country list in the published guidelines
Count every team member's years of professional conservation experience - none may exceed five
Write a capacity-development role for each team member, as the guidelines require it
Design a six-to-12-month project with measurable conservation action, not research alone, mapped to one of the eight themes
Build a budget in which the CLP request is no more than US$15,000 and CLP funds at least 50% of the total
Email the completed concept note template to clp.applications@birdlife.org before 23:59 GMT on 30 October 2026
common_rejection_risks: A team member with more than five years of professional conservation experience
Fewer than three team members, or no explanation of how each member develops capacity
A project that reads as pure academic research rather than applied conservation
A project country missing from the guidelines' eligible-country list
A CLP share below 50% of the budget or a request above US$15,000
A late or incomplete email submission, which is excluded outright
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: At least 50% of the total project budget must be met from sources other than CLP.
document_audit: The concept note must be completed on the downloadable CLP template and follow the published guidelines; free-form proposals are not the Stage 1 product
Incomplete or ineligible Stage 1 submissions are not considered, so internal review before the email matters more than speed
Stage 2 guidelines reach only shortlisted teams, so budget and team planning cannot wait for them
alerts: The Stage 1 deadline is an email deadline - 23:59 GMT on Friday 30 October 2026 - with no portal in stage one
Only the highest-scoring concept notes are invited to Stage 2, and that invitation comes with its own unpublished timing
The 2027 process differs from previous years, so old concept-note habits may not fit the new two-stage format
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Email the concept note to clp.applications@birdlife.org by the Stage 1 deadline; CLP scores concept notes against the eligibility criteria and the eight themes, notifies shortlisted teams, and those teams submit a full application through the CLP online portal.
